newsitem.title: CHINA: Vessels collide in southwest China, 42 drown.
newsitem.headline: Vessels collide in southwest China, 42 drown.

text.p: Forty-two people drowned when an overloaded passenger ship sank after colliding head-on with a freighter in thick fog in southwest China last week, a government official said on Monday.
Owners of the two vessels have been taken into police custody, the official told Reuters by telephone.
The vessels collided on Tuojiang river in Sichuan province on January 3, the official said, adding that rescue workers had recovered 42 bodies and rescued 20 people.
"Heavy fog and overloading caused the accident," he said.
The passenger ship had a seating capacity of 42 people but was carrying 60 people when it collided with the freighter and sank, the official said.
The freighter was carrying 40 tonnes of sand, or 15 tonnes more than capacity, he said.
